title: Sort Numbers in Ascending Order
description: Read N integers and print them in ascending order, separated by single spaces.
input_format: First N (1 ≤ N ≤ 1000), followed by N integers.
output_format: Print all N integers in non-decreasing order on one line.

starter_code.Python:
n = int(input())
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))
numbers.sort()
print(" ".join(map(str, numbers[:n])))

learning_content.title: Sorting and ordering
learning_content.intro: Sorting arranges values in a requested order. Ascending order means every element is less than or equal to the element that follows it.
points: Store all values in an array or list.
Apply a sorting algorithm or library sort.
Print the sorted values with spaces between them.
Preserve repeated values; sorting does not remove duplicates.
learning_content.complexity: O(n log n) time for the supplied library-sort approaches; O(n²) for the C bubble-sort starter · O(n) or implementation-dependent extra space
learning_content.note: The C starter uses bubble sort for clarity; the other language starters use standard library sorting.

quiz.question: What does ascending order require for each adjacent pair in the sorted output?

options.label: The left value is greater than the right value
The left value is less than or equal to the right value
options.feedback: This is the non-decreasing condition for ascending order.

options.label: All values must be distinct
options.feedback: Sorting preserves duplicates; uniqueness is not required.

options.label: All negative values must be removed
options.feedback: Sorting changes order, not which values are included.

quiz.explanation: Ascending non-decreasing order satisfies a[i] <= a[i+1] for every adjacent pair.
